candidate_proposition: If competing providers can demonstrate quality only after users grant scarce exclusive integrations, competition can shift toward securing early integrations rather than improving demonstrated service, even with free profile export.
strongest_interpretation: If demonstrating agent quality requires scarce exclusive integrations, provider competition can concentrate audition opportunities even with free data portability. Nonexclusive trials can alter quality investment without changing switching price.

closest_works.title: Competition in Persuasion
closest_works.prior_proposition: Competition need not improve information. A condition on feasible experiments determines when more informative outcomes are guaranteed; sequential and costly information introduce further limits.

comparison.same_variables: Partly: feasible experiments differ across providers.

comparison.same_outcome: Information quality rather than formal integration ownership.
comparison.same_prediction: Competition cannot guarantee information under arbitrary information environments.
comparison.same_intervention: Expand connected feasible experiments; not just add senders.
